TIER A VERIFICATION PASS — COMPLETE (2026-08-13 → 2026-08-23)

Every Tier A lead has now had its decision-maker and phone independently verified against state records (Sunbiz first), company statements, and current news. Starting position: 66 Tier A leads (24 verified, 42 pending). Final position: 54 Tier A leads — 53 Verified, 1 pending (#106 Antillean Marine: phone and family ownership confirmed; president’s name requires one phone call — never guess a name into a call). 12 leads were removed from Tier A under the disposition rule (acquired / PE-controlled / foreign-owned / defunct): 11 downgraded to C, and 1 (#164 Natalie’s) reclassified to B because the acquirer is itself a family operator.

Corrections that mattered: Wish Farms (#146) changed CEOs 2026-06-01 — James Peterson now CEO, Gary Wishnatzki Chairman; outreach addressed to the old structure would have failed in the first line. Three stale directory listings were overridden by Sunbiz (TruckMax, Barney’s Pumps, Sunshine Bouquet). Rulon (#92) lost its founder Feb 2025 — CFO Caleb Diffell now CEO with the Robison family still in leadership; post-succession timing favors outside costing help.

Pattern findings: (1) Consolidation has gutted Tampa Bay industrial distribution — every distributor on the original list there was acquired or PE-recapped within ~4 years; treat the metro as a consolidation-target market, not an independent-operator market. (2) The family-owned block (#105–195) held at a ~74% survival rate vs ~33% in Tampa Bay — ownership-curated sourcing beats industry-curated sourcing. (3) Directory data (BBB, aggregators) runs 2–8 years stale on principals; Sunbiz annual reports were decisive in every disputed case. (4) Two verified leads carry standing cautions: Morgan Auto (#141, active litigation — do not initiate) and Arthrex (#125, far above size range).

Remaining work outside Tier A: phone-number lookups flagged on 8 verified rows; #106 identity call; Tier B sweep (now 98 leads incl. Natalie’s and the McNichols Tier-B option) unstarted.

Pre-Check & Verification Pass Summary — FINAL, 2026-08-24

State of the file: Tier A: 52 Verified, 0 pending — pass complete. Net moves: BlueGrace and Morgan Auto downgraded A→B (undetected PE sponsor stakes: Warburg Pincus $255M/2016; Greenbriar + scale + litigation). #106 Antillean verified (Sara Babun, 2nd gen) with a hard ownership-litigation caution — control itself contested in a multi-year sibling estate war; confirm status before any approach.

Pre-check results (five checks, whole file)

(1) Row-number uniqueness: CLEAN — 200 rows, 1–200, no duplicates or gaps; Florida escaped the Chicago duplicate-number defect class. (2) City-match: 11 Tier A rows lacked FL phone/address anchors; all 11 searched and anchored — no wrong-state phantoms found; anchors now call-ready. (3) Trading-name retry: standing rule, no unfindable rows this pass. (4) Shared-parentage: two candidate pairs (Brown ×2, Sunshine ×2) adjudicated unrelated — no duplicate parents. (5) Cap-table check (NEW, Tim-ratified this pass): search ownership independently of leadership — a founder in the CEO seat proves nothing about who controls the capital budget. Result: 2 of 11 anchor rows carried undetected sponsor money (BlueGrace, Morgan) — earlier passes systematically under-detected PE because founder-still-present read as founder-owned. Massey shows the counter-rule: when a PRIMARY source (company's own 2025 "largest privately-owned family company" claim) contradicts an aggregator PE round, the primary source wins pending a call.

New findings for the cross-market taxonomy

Comparison-page data bleed (new aggregator-noise signature): CBInsights' side-by-side view leaked Dairy Queen's investors (Berkshire Hathaway) and CEO into Bubba Foods' column — produces plausible-looking wrong answers, not obvious garbage. Also: PitchBook landmine on Morgan ("acquired by Pinewood Technologies 2021" — a DMS venture misrecorded as a sale of the group). Deceased-principal count grows: Massey founder Harvey Massey (d. 2024, caught this pass) and Antillean co-founder Jose Babun Selman. Ownership-tag correction: Bubba Foods is Morris-owned since 2000, not founder-family.

Florida call-list top tier

1) IMG Citrus (ADDED per Tim 2026-08-24) — three signals in one row: fresh three-sibling co-CEO generational handover, ~$90M parent across three business lines (citrus/landscape/real estate), and acquiring assets (2,500-ac ex-Chiquita grove + cold storage) while the FL citrus industry contracts. 2) Rulon — post-founder succession, family chair + professional CEO (Sunbiz-confirmed). Strong family rows with fresh anchors: El Dorado (Capó board), Miami Beef (Young family in every officer seat), Milam's (13 family members, 6 doors), Detwiler's. Hard cautions: Antillean (ownership litigation), Morgan Auto (B: sponsor + litigation), Massey (enterprise scale — division-level angle only, and resolve the aggregator PE claim at dial).
